# [TASK] Tests and accessibility pass: query highlighting

## Task
Test and accessibility pass for query highlighting.

## Parent Story
Parent: #199

## Scope
Coverage gaps left after Tasks #1-#3's own inline tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Component tests cover all three highlight categories rendering simultaneously in one query — already covered by `QueryHighlightOverlay.test.jsx`'s existing "renders three categories in one query..." test; unchanged by this Task.
- [x] Dictated-query highlighting (transcript populates the field) is covered, not just typed input — required fixing a real gap first: `VoiceControl.jsx`'s "search" voice command never populated `Search.jsx`'s own field state at all, it ran the search itself and bypassed the highlighting pipeline entirely, so there was nothing to write a test *for*. Wired a one-shot Redux hand-off (`dictatedQuery`/`dictatedQuerySubmitted`/`dictatedQueryConsumed` in `currentGenreOrCategory.js`) so a dictated query now runs through `Search.jsx`'s own `runParse`/`runSearch` pipeline exactly as a typed-and-Entered query would. This also satisfies parent Story #199's own AC5. 5 new tests in `Search.test.jsx` cover field population, immediate (non-debounced) parsing, overlay rendering, empty-query parity with `handleKeyPress`'s own empty-Enter branch, one-shot consumption, debounce-cancellation, and the out-of-order-response race between two back-to-back dictated queries — plus the search-execution itself is now asserted (verified by deliberately deleting the `runSearch()` call and confirming the test suite goes red).
- [x] Automated accessibility check (e.g. axe) confirms highlighting isn't conveyed by color alone — added `jest-axe`, registered globally in `setupTests.js`; new test in `QueryHighlightOverlay.test.jsx` runs `axe()` against all three categories rendered together. (axe-core has no rule that can itself judge "color alone" — that's a WCAG 1.4.1 visual-design question — so this guards against any *other* accessibility violation the highlighted markup introduces; the "not color alone" property itself is what the pre-existing `textDecorationStyle`/`fontWeight` assertions prove.)
- [x] Manual check: highlighting legible in both light and dark mode — verified with a real Chromium screenshot of the actual search field (all three categories, "a and not Batman") in both themes via the dev server. Dark mode renders `highlightStyles.js`'s three colors as designed and clearly legible. Light mode passes every overlay pixel through this field's pre-existing `filter: invert(1)` hack, which inverts the three underline colors too — they land on a different but still three mutually-distinct, legible hue triplet against the light-mode field's blue background. Both themes stay distinguishable by underline shape (dotted/wavy/solid) and weight, not just color.

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4 (actual: ~2x — AC2 required fixing the underlying dictation-to-field wiring gap described above, not just writing tests against existing behavior)
